priority_scheme.P0: Blocks safe foundational or release work

features.description: Production-oriented vertical application scaffold
acceptance_criteria: Compose builds and all three services become healthy
Backend readiness verifies PostgreSQL and frontend reaches the API through its proxy
Migrations, persistence across container recreation, tests, static checks, and backup validation pass

features.description: Exercise restore against an isolated disposable database
acceptance_criteria: A custom-format dump restores into an isolated database
Migration revision and infrastructure metadata match the source
The drill and cleanup procedure are documented without touching valuable data

features.description: Audit repository consistency and public-repository readiness
acceptance_criteria: Public and engineering documentation accurately distinguish implemented behavior from planned capabilities through PLANT-004
Installation, development, upgrade, backup, contribution, security, and repository metadata guidance is consistent with executable configuration
Feature dependencies, internal links, documentation formatting, and the unchanged application verification suite pass, with unresolved release decisions reported

features.description: Run Florabase verification automatically on pull requests
acceptance_criteria: Pull requests run frontend and backend formatting, lint, strict typing, and unit or component tests
PostgreSQL integration tests and generated API drift checks run in an isolated repeatable environment
Production image builds run where practical and failures are visible without weakening local verification

features.description: Add deterministic feature verification and protected delivery tooling
acceptance_criteria: A canonical feature verification command runs each local pull-request-equivalent gate once, validates repository tooling and the feature graph, checks whitespace errors, and records only machine-local evidence for the verified working tree
Feature branches adding Alembic revisions receive a previous-main-head to feature-head downgrade/re-upgrade cycle in a disposable PostgreSQL environment without touching development data

A fail-closed delivery command verifies the exact reviewed commit, performs only a normal push, reuses or creates one pull request, validates current-SHA required checks, enables exact-SHA squash auto-merge, and reports migration follow-up without local cleanup or database mutation
Focused no-network helper tests cover verification orchestration, migration detection, delivery safety preconditions, current-SHA check handling, PR reuse, and terminal delivery states

features.description: Consolidate development, dirty-worktree review, stable preview and production workflows
acceptance_criteria: Existing Codex worktrees initialize without another worktree or switching primary main; linked finish preserves primary index/source safety and per-worktree verification receipts include dirty and untracked source

DEV, Feature Review, Stable Preview, quality, integration and production have explicit source/config/project/resource contracts, observable health and migration current/head, and ahead-of-code refusal without automatic downgrade

A real linked-worktree Compose smoke proves isolated dirty migrations, noninteractive non-root frontend dependency bootstrap, root-owned volume repair, stop/restart persistence, safe scoped removal and unchanged DEV

Canonical operator commands, review profiles, lifecycle documentation and actionable delivery diagnostics pass focused helper coverage and the final verification gate; paired DEV data cloning and public-image distribution remain deferred

features.description: Provide an isolated persistent operator Preview for UAT
acceptance_criteria: Operator UAT Preview uses the current dirty/untracked feature worktree through Feature Review isolation primitives, with persistent DB/media/dependencies distinct from DEV, Stable Preview and production; source, health, database/code migration state and fixture identity are observable

A UAT-only preview/preview owner and bounded synthetic collection are created explicitly through host resource, runtime, origin and actual database identity guards; normal production/DEV/Stable Preview startup and authentication remain unchanged

Versioned UUIDv7 fixture identities make repeated seed idempotent and preserve operator edits; interrupted, missing or incompatible baselines refuse with guarded reset instructions, without matching mutable names or adding production domain fields

Simple uat-preview-up, uat-preview-stop, uat-preview-status, uat-preview-seed, uat-preview-reset and uat-preview-remove commands remain distinct from existing Stable Preview commands; startup never seeds, stop/start preserves state, and reset deletes only individually validated UAT resources with exact confirmation; owning-worktree removal stops writers and retires only exact UAT containers/network/volumes without rebuilding or editing Git/source, so the next feature starts and seeds fresh state

Real uniquely isolated Compose smoke covers fresh/empty startup, real owner login, runtime guard refusals, repeat seed, fixture/media/lineage relationships, operator edits, DB/media/dependency persistence, forward migrations and ahead refusal, reset, old-owner removal followed by new-feature fresh startup/seed/login and before/after unchanged operator environments; operator UAT and independent canonical verification complete acceptance

features.description: Harden and validate the first distributable Florabase 0.1.0 release
acceptance_criteria: A clean installation and an upgrade from a supported pre-release installation complete through production Compose and the full Alembic upgrade chain; health and readiness, owner bootstrap, login, logout, session restoration, and browser use after upgrade are verified under production-safe configuration

A complete supported backup pairs PostgreSQL data with local attachment storage; an isolated restore proves collection records, relationships, media binaries, and application use without modifying valuable operator data or presenting a database-only dump as complete recovery

Representative end-to-end collection UAT follows BotanicalIdentity through optional profile or cover, acquisition and provenance, SeedLot, Sowing, Plant or PlantGroup, Events, Photos, transfer or extraction, supported reversal or reintegration, maps, and history navigation

Security and failure review covers session expiry or invalidation where practical, CSRF, exact Origin checks, attachment and binary authorization, production cookie and origin settings, existing insecure-configuration startup rejection, API and provider failures, external-image failure, missing media, validation conflicts, empty data, and implemented stale-source states

Desktop, intermediate-width, and approximately 390 by 844 mobile review covers keyboard use, visible focus, dialogs, menus, forms, maps with companion lists, and important error, empty, and loading states without claiming formal accessibility certification; final release-candidate resource sanity checks documented PERF-001 expectations, material regressions, and obvious runaway CPU, memory, or request behavior rather than repeating the primary optimization project

Installation, persistence, backup, restore, upgrade, configuration, and map documentation matches the release tree; application version 0.1.0, pre-1.0 version and upgrade expectations, coherent exposed version surfaces, and the first changelog entry are recorded; stale current-state prose and concrete release defects are resolved before the exact release tree passes canonical verification

features.description: Measure and optimize Florabase resource efficiency for self-hosted deployment
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible production-like baseline documents idle and representative operator workflows: startup and an idle authenticated session; Dashboard; BotanicalIdentity, SeedLot, Sowing, Plant or PlantGroup, Supplier, Location, and Geography directories and details; Events, Photos, lineage, provenance map, explicitly loaded occurrence map, and representative create or edit work. The workload measures process or container CPU and memory, startup stabilization, frontend initial transfer and lazy chunks, API and important database query counts, representative response time, media and map loading, and production image and process footprint where practical without relying only on synthetic microbenchmarks

Measured backend and PostgreSQL hotspots are reviewed for N+1 or redundant queries, unnecessary serialization or payload, repeated expensive queries, connection and memory behavior, and representative query plans; indexes or tuning are added only when workload evidence and appropriate EXPLAIN or ANALYZE support them, without speculative denormalization, materialized views, or generic tuning

Measured frontend, media, and map hotspots are reviewed for production bundle and chunk cost, the existing Vite chunk-size advisory, useful code splitting and lazy loading, unnecessary renders or duplicate API requests, oversized original images where bounded thumbnails fit, lazy local and external Photos behavior, hidden map instances, and map or provider traffic on unrelated navigation; the advisory threshold is not raised merely to hide a warning

Repeated navigation and extended idle use are checked for event-listener, map-instance, timer, request, retained-data, client-cache, session, and database-connection growth; CPU, memory, and requests stabilize without unnecessary polling or render loops, and only demonstrated leaks or resource hotspots are changed without altering domain semantics, security, or privacy or adding broad caching infrastructure

The production Compose stack is assessed for modest self-hosted hardware using measured CPU, memory, network, database, image-size, startup, package, process, and duplicate-work costs; footprint changes preserve reproducible builds, security updates, and needed operability, with no arbitrary hardware guarantee set before measurement

After focused optimization, the same representative workload is re-measured against the baseline; material improvements, remaining costs, practical small-installation resource expectations, and any meaningful regressions across measured dimensions are documented, with evidence-based regression budgets added only where justified

features.description: Decide the initial authentication and session architecture
acceptance_criteria: Single-operator and multi-user exposure assumptions are documented
Reverse-proxy identity and application-session options are compared
The backend-owned session, cookie, CSRF, password, bootstrap, invalidation, lifetime, and abuse-control decisions are explicit
Proxy, HTTPS, CORS, API failure, configuration, database, and deferred boundaries are testable
An accepted ADR records the chosen boundary and required protections without fake authentication

features.description: Implement local owner authentication and server-side sessions
acceptance_criteria: Alembic-managed user, session, and bounded login-throttle persistence follows ADR 0005
The guarded first-owner CLI, Argon2id login, session rotation/revocation, logout, and expiry behavior are integration-tested
Secure cookie, same-origin, CSRF, generic failure, authorization-default, rate-limit, and secret-redaction behavior are tested
Production fails closed for insecure origin, cookie, CORS, or required authentication configuration

features.description: Define the first BotanicalIdentity aggregate contract
acceptance_criteria: Real user workflows and minimum fields are documented
BotanicalIdentity, scientific taxon name, cultivar qualifier, shared scope, and duplicate reconciliation boundaries are explicit
The change remains small enough for one migration and API increment

features.description: Add the minimal BotanicalIdentity schema through Alembic
acceptance_criteria: Migration uses UUIDv7 identifiers, UTC timestamps, and justified constraints
Upgrade and downgrade are tested against PostgreSQL
No unrelated botanical tables are introduced

features.description: Expose the first validated BotanicalIdentity REST slice
acceptance_criteria: Versioned create and read behavior follows the documented contract
Validation, conflicts, not-found behavior, and database constraints are tested
OpenAPI and generated frontend types are current

features.description: Build the browser owner login, session, and logout flow
acceptance_criteria: Accessible login uses the generated backend API contract and presents generic credential or throttle failures with explicit loading and failure states
An authenticated browser session is restored after reload, including a safe way to obtain a usable session-bound CSRF token without re-entering the password
Logout is supported without storing authentication tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage or weakening the HttpOnly session-cookie boundary

features.description: Build the first accessible BotanicalIdentity interaction
acceptance_criteria: The UI uses generated API declarations
Loading, empty, success, validation, and server-error states are explicit
Keyboard and accessible-name behavior has component coverage

features.description: Add the basic BotanicalIdentity directory and navigation workflow
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated users can retrieve a deterministic directory of existing BotanicalIdentity records without knowing their UUIDs
The accessible frontend supports browsing/selecting an existing BotanicalIdentity and reuses its existing detail/profile interaction
Creation, duplicate handling, loading, empty, selection, authentication, and failure behavior remain explicit without introducing advanced collection search

features.description: Decide persistent attachment metadata and storage boundaries
acceptance_criteria: Relationship, filename, type, size, validation, deletion, and backup semantics are documented
Volume ownership and reverse-proxy upload limits are defined
No object storage is introduced without a concrete requirement

features.description: Add a PostgreSQL-backed API integration test fixture
acceptance_criteria: Tests use an isolated disposable database
Migrations initialize the schema and cleanup cannot target non-test data
The integration command is documented and works in Compose

features.description: Define the first manually maintained BotanicalProfile contract
acceptance_criteria: The contract keeps general botanical knowledge separate from BotanicalIdentity and collection observations
A small incomplete-friendly first profile is defined without one field per possible botanical fact
Operator-authored content and later source-scoped enrichment boundaries are explicit

features.description: Add the first protected manual BotanicalProfile interaction
acceptance_criteria: An Alembic-managed profile references exactly one BotanicalIdentity and permits incomplete content
Authenticated create, read, and update behavior is validated and integration-tested
The accessible UI distinguishes reference knowledge from collection observations

features.description: External botanical data foundation
acceptance_criteria: A narrow backend provider boundary uses GBIF as the first fixed provider, normalizes documented Catalogue of Life eXtended Release search and match results, and translates bounded network, rate-limit, not-found, and malformed-response failures without exposing provider response shapes or arbitrary URLs

Authenticated BotanicalIdentity workflows search advisory candidates and require explicit operator confirmation before creating or replacing at most one current provider link, while unlink and refresh retain Florabase-owned identity and profile data unchanged

Alembic-managed relational provider links retain opaque external IDs and link-time provenance, while a concurrency-safe PostgreSQL response cache records payload and fetch time under a configurable freshness policy without becoming canonical botanical data

The accessible responsive BotanicalIdentity UI exposes unlinked, search, ambiguous-candidate, linked, stale, refresh-failure, change, and unlink states with trusted GBIF references and no automatic taxonomy correction, profile enrichment, native-range import, or occurrence mapping

features.description: Botanical profile enrichment
acceptance_criteria: Only explicitly reviewed source records may propose description: WFO / Flora of China remains blocked pending secure current verification, while Kew SEPASAL / Flora Zambesiaca TaxKey/NoteKey/BiblKey 78/104262/5701, 624/98287/5701 and 1152/98358/5701 are approved under CC BY 4.0; these three records are insufficient coverage for general enrichment. Kew WCVP geographic_area may propose origin_distribution. Fixed backend retrieval and exact provider-specific identity confirmation never modify profile or identity data during retrieval

Empty fields require explicit Apply, while populated fields require Current vs Proposed review and concrete Replace confirmation; unrelated profile fields and operator-managed structured native ranges remain unchanged

Typed relational append-only application history retains field, nullable previous value, applied value, provider, dataset, exact record/reference, licence, attribution, retrieval time, release fingerprint and application time/operator where available

Field-specific current provenance identifies the enrichment application without string comparison; manual edits clear only the edited field association while preserving history, and equivalent current value/source evidence avoids duplicate application rows

Transactional apply rejects stale destination or proposal/source-version review; refresh, failure, disappearance, cache expiry and source-link changes preserve canonical applied text and historical evidence

Accessible responsive Profile review exposes proposals, concrete confirmation, current attribution and field-level history with reviewed licence/reference credit; any source outside the exact approved records requires its own source review and secure retrieval, without TLS bypass or unreviewed source paths
After successful independent identity creation an optional botanical-information review and Skip are available; existing identities support explicit later trusted-source checks without recreation

Missing optional local sources leave ordinary startup and manual profile editing usable; descriptions and geographic_area text are never fabricated from taxonomy, occurrences, structured native assertions or drawing geometry

features.description: Add a reusable Supplier and acquisition-source directory
acceptance_criteria: Supplier supports seller, nursery, supermarket, person, exchange, and other source workflows without requiring geographic origin
Protected persistence and API behavior preserve optional contact or descriptive data
The accessible UI supports selecting and maintaining suppliers independently of lots

features.description: Add a simple hierarchical collection Location directory
acceptance_criteria: Locations support an optional parent and prevent hierarchy cycles
Protected persistence and API behavior cover roots, children, rename, and safe retirement
The accessible UI can choose a location for stored material or cultivated plants

features.description: Add hierarchical GeographicPlace reference data
acceptance_criteria: GeographicPlace is distinct from collection Location and supports canonical World, continent, applicable subregion, and country or territory nodes from documented maintained standards and codes
Relationships select the most appropriate known node and infer ancestors without manufacturing precision or redundantly persisting every ancestor
Canonical base nodes remain stable reference data, while operator-defined local places can extend them without introducing coordinates, GIS, maps, or external runtime geography integrations

features.description: Structured botanical native ranges
acceptance_criteria: Structured native range uses the shared GeographicPlace hierarchy and remains independent from SeedLot material provenance
A BotanicalIdentity or profile may reference one or more broad or precise known places without replacing disjunct areas with their common ancestor
Existing operator-authored BotanicalProfile origin_distribution text remains valid and is not silently overwritten

features.description: Define the SeedLot and seed provenance contract
acceptance_criteria: One physical packet or bag is one SeedLot referencing BotanicalIdentity even when descriptive details match another lot
Acquisition and harvest dates preserve known precision, and optional quantity supports exact or approximate count or weight
Source category, optional Supplier, optional geographic origin, storage, notes, lifecycle, and later parent-Plant lineage boundaries are explicit

features.description: Persist the first SeedLot inventory slice
acceptance_criteria: One focused Alembic increment follows the approved SeedLot contract and references BotanicalIdentity, Supplier, GeographicPlace material provenance, and Location where present
PostgreSQL constraints preserve optionality, declared date precision, quantity kind, and non-destructive lifecycle states
Upgrade, downgrade, and database invariants are integration-tested without introducing Sowing or Plant tables

features.description: Expose the protected SeedLot API workflow
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated create, read, list, update, and lifecycle behavior follows the SeedLot contract
Validation covers partial dates, optional exact or approximate quantity, source, supplier, origin, and location independently
Failures, authorization, and historical retention are integration-tested and generated API artifacts are current

features.description: Build the first accessible SeedLot inventory UI
acceptance_criteria: Fast entry requires only integrity-critical information and does not imply unknown date or quantity precision
List and detail views distinguish inactive lots while retaining their history
Loading, empty, success, validation, and failure states have component coverage

features.description: Define the Sowing and basic germination contract
acceptance_criteria: A Sowing represents material intentionally taken from exactly one SeedLot
Fast entry has a small minimum while substrate, method, treatment, temperature, and environment remain optional
Simple sown and germinated totals coexist with later optional dated germination observations

features.description: Add the protected Sowing and basic germination backend slice
acceptance_criteria: Alembic-managed Sowings reference SeedLots and retain failed or completed outcomes
Authenticated API behavior supports quick entry, optional cultivation details, and simple germination totals
Quantity integrity, failures, and historical retention are integration-tested

features.description: Build the accessible Sowing and basic germination UI
acceptance_criteria: The primary flow records a Sowing and simple germination result with minimal input
Advanced optional details are available without blocking simple use
Active, failed, and completed Sowings remain discoverable with tested loading and failure states

features.description: Define individual Plant and PlantGroup contracts
acceptance_criteria: Individually tracked specimens and grouped batches are distinct concepts with shared workflow lineage
Origin, optional location, quantity for groups, and historical lifecycle outcomes are explicit
Individual extraction preserves group provenance but its transaction details remain deferred

features.description: Add the protected Plant and PlantGroup backend slice
acceptance_criteria: Alembic-managed Plants and PlantGroups preserve their BotanicalIdentity and originating Sowing where known
Authenticated API behavior supports individual and group lifecycle and location changes without destructive deletion
Group quantity, provenance, authorization, and inactive-state invariants are integration-tested

features.description: Build the accessible Plant and PlantGroup collection UI
acceptance_criteria: The UI supports choosing individual or group tracking from a successful Sowing
Current location and active or historical state are visible without hiding provenance
Loading, empty, validation, success, and failure states have component coverage

features.description: Define explicit collection-workflow lineage relationships
acceptance_criteria: The contract covers SeedLot to Sowing to Plant or PlantGroup and parent Plant to collection-produced SeedLot
Known provenance is retained while unknown links remain optional
No generic graph, genealogy engine, or speculative relationship type is introduced

features.description: Complete collection-producer lineage and supported traversal
acceptance_criteria: A SeedLot produced in the collection can reference its one known Plant or PlantGroup producer
The API can traverse the explicit upstream and downstream workflow relationships
Lineage survives inactive lifecycle states and is covered by integration tests

features.description: Define the lightweight Plant history and observation contract
acceptance_criteria: The first vocabulary covers movement, repotting, flowering, fruiting, pruning, treatment, harvest, death or loss, and free observations without separate tables per type
Events retain when and what happened with partial information allowed
Collection observations remain separate from BotanicalProfile reference knowledge

features.description: Add a lightweight protected Plant history timeline
acceptance_criteria: Plants and PlantGroups can retain typed events and free observations in chronological history
Location and lifecycle events preserve prior history rather than overwriting it
Authenticated API and accessible timeline behavior cover validation, failure, and inactive records

features.description: Implement guarded local attachment storage
acceptance_criteria: Alembic metadata and configured durable storage follow the accepted ATTACHMENT-001 boundaries
Upload and retrieval validate size, filename, media type, authorization, and trusted storage roots
Backup, restore, deletion, and failure behavior are integration-tested and documented

features.description: Relate photos to collection records and add an optional BotanicalIdentity cover
acceptance_criteria: Locally managed photos and external image references use distinct semantics and explicit supported relationships to SeedLot, Sowing, Plant, PlantGroup, or justified collection events

The UI distinguishes uploaded content from source URLs and exposes captions, attribution, broken-link or loading failures, and privacy-safe external-media behavior without implying unsupported generic attachment targets

Inactive collection records retain their photo history and remain usable without images, while each BotanicalIdentity may independently have one optional local or operator-approved external representative cover without becoming a collection-photo target

Identity covers support safe replacement and removal but no version history, automatic discovery, provider search, albums or reordering, EXIF inspection, thumbnails, derivatives, background media workers, compact directory rendering, or BotanicalIdentity gallery

features.description: Add an explicit primary photo for selected collection records
acceptance_criteria: SeedLot, Plant and PlantGroup may each optionally designate one existing associated collection photo as the primary representative photo; Sowing is outside this scope
Primary selection is explicit operator intent; Florabase never automatically chooses the first, newest or only photo
Changing or removing the designation preserves photo history; deleting or removing the primary photo clears or safely resolves the designation without dangling references
Directories and details may use a bounded representation of the explicitly selected primary photo without loading full-size originals or changing BotanicalIdentity cover semantics

features.description: Introduce reusable MediaAssets, record links and a central Media library
acceptance_criteria: Local and external MediaAssets may remain fully unreferenced; unlinking never deletes an asset and explicit deletion is blocked by collection links or BotanicalIdentity cover references

RecordMediaLinks retain exact supported SeedLot, Sowing, Plant, PlantGroup and Event targets, independent captions and order; primary selection remains explicit and limited to SeedLot, Plant and PlantGroup
A data-preserving Alembic migration retains originals, metadata, photo and cover relationships, privacy and primary selections with an explicit guarded downgrade policy
Paginated Media directory and detail, record Link existing media, multi-record association and precise unlink versus asset-delete workflows are accessible and responsive
Authenticated file and shared thumbnail access, external opt-in privacy, relational integrity, concurrent mutations and batched directory summaries are tested

External references support explicit persistent Save, Refresh and Remove local copy; protected saved content is preferred across views, failures retain valid snapshots, SSRF and concurrency boundaries are tested, and snapshots participate in backup/restore
Canonical verification, rendered review and basic query, storage and resource evidence are recorded

features.description: Record structured Harvest occurrences with ordered material lines and shared media
acceptance_criteria: Harvest requires exactly one retained Plant or PlantGroup source, one or more ordered material lines, and reuses partial occurrence dates without denormalizing identity or Location
Controlled materials and optional positive count or weight quantities preserve exact, approximate and unknown precision without inventory or lifecycle side effects

Atomic aggregate creation, correction including source changes, and deletion keep exactly one explicitly owned harvest Event coherent; ordinary Event mutation is protected and free-form historical harvest Events remain unchanged

Harvest supports reusable MediaAsset links, target-specific captions/order and explicit primary images; unlink/deletion retains shared assets and safe visual fallback resolves direct primary, source and identity context
Harvest directory, search/material/source filters, compact preview, aggregate forms, detail, contextual source actions and identity collection history are accessible and responsive
Dashboard and Event history link to structured Harvest details without duplicate Events or media links and without adding historical Harvests to current holdings

PostgreSQL enforces source, item, owned Event and primary-link integrity; guarded migration, rollback, retention, permissions, bounded queries, tests, rendered review and canonical verification have recorded evidence
Future harvested-material inventory/disposition and explicit conversion to SeedLot remain documented pre-1.0 follow-ups

features.description: Manage stored harvested material and explicit disposition history
acceptance_criteria: Explicit opt-in creates at most one current inventory per HarvestItem without backfill or rewriting collected quantities; exact, approximate and unknown current quantities remain independent
Active/depleted state, optional scope-compatible storage Location and ordinary current-state correction preserve historical Harvest and disposition facts

Consumed, processed, discarded, gifted and used_for_propagation dispositions atomically retain typed before/after snapshots; exact partial usage derives a positive compatible remainder, approximate usage requires confirmed approximate remainder, unknown stays unknown and explicit use-all depletes

Fresh owner/inventory locks serialize competing disposition, correction and source-mutation requests; restrictive relational guards retain source context and block deletion or material-kind changes while tracked

Stored material is a peer Harvest workspace view with distinct collected/remaining labels, focused tracking/disposition/correction forms and retained accessible history across desktop, tablet and mobile
Inventory directory and direct/descendant-inclusive Location projections use bounded batched queries; depleted inventory is excluded from current active counts and retained in totals
Authenticated reads and owner/CSRF/exact-Origin mutations use generated authoritative contracts; migration has no backfill and guards populated downgrade while empty downgrade/re-upgrade works
No source lifecycle or Event effects, lineage edge, SeedLot conversion, propagation record/receipt, new media target, global-search expansion or generic inventory framework is introduced

features.description: Add dated germination observations and derived statistics
acceptance_criteria: Optional dated observations can coexist with simple germination totals
Percentage, first germination, timing, cumulative germination, and T50 are derived only when sufficient data exists
Missing observations never prevent basic Sowing use

features.description: Make the authenticated Florabase web app installable as a safe mobile PWA
acceptance_criteria: A valid manifest, supported application icons, standalone display behavior, HTTPS requirements, and installability are implemented and tested on the supported mobile-browser targets

Service-worker and cache behavior has an explicit safe policy that does not accidentally persist authenticated API responses, session material, or stale mutation results, and application updates have clear user-visible behavior

Initial PWA scope provides installability and reliable application-shell behavior without claiming offline mutation/synchronization, push notifications, or native-device integrations that have not been separately designed

features.description: Add purchase Orders distinct from Suppliers and material lots
acceptance_criteria: An Order groups an acquisition transaction without merging separate physical lots
Optional price, date, supplier, and order-reference data preserve known precision
SeedLots can link to an Order without requiring all lots to be purchased

features.description: Deepen PlantEvent workflows from observed usage
acceptance_criteria: Structured event details are added only for event types with demonstrated filtering or workflow needs
Existing lightweight events and free observations remain valid
History remains chronological, attributable, and non-destructive

features.description: Extract an individual Plant from a PlantGroup
acceptance_criteria: Extraction atomically reduces the active group quantity and creates one individual Plant
The individual preserves its direct originating PlantGroup relationship and derivable upstream Sowing and SeedLot provenance while BotanicalIdentity remains independently correctable
Invalid quantities, concurrent extraction, and historical-group behavior are integration-tested

features.description: Add a TuberLot workflow parallel to SeedLot
acceptance_criteria: One physical tuber lot retains BotanicalIdentity, source, quantity, location, lifecycle, and provenance
Establishment into Plants or PlantGroups preserves lineage without using Sowing
No generic propagation-material base table is introduced without demonstrated need

features.description: Add a CuttingLot workflow parallel to SeedLot
acceptance_criteria: One physical cutting lot retains BotanicalIdentity, source, quantity, location, lifecycle, and provenance
Rooting or establishment into Plants or PlantGroups preserves known parent-Plant lineage without using Sowing
The implementation follows concrete cutting workflows rather than speculative inheritance

features.description: Add printable labels and QR-based record lookup
acceptance_criteria: Labels identify supported collection records with stable, non-secret references
QR lookup requires normal authorization and does not encode session credentials
QR URLs use the configured canonical origin and existing detail routes, independent of the browser Host
Printable output is tested for the selected physical label workflow

features.description: Add advanced collection search and filtering
acceptance_criteria: Filters reflect implemented structured fields and lifecycle states rather than speculative metadata
Botanical reference knowledge and collection observations remain distinguishable in results
Empty, partial, authorized, and large-result behavior is tested

features.description: Complete global search coverage for Harvests and Media
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated Dashboard global search includes typed Harvest and Media kinds with stable IDs and exact detail routes
Harvest text matches explicit label, derived source title, exact source identity names, notes and material kind/description without Location, Supplier or provenance inference
Harvest identity and occurrence PartialDate year filters apply; unrelated relationships, lifecycle and Event kind do not apply
Media text reuses direct Library title, original filename and attribution semantics without linked-record or cover inference
Mixed kinds retain deterministic groups, exact totals and bounded pagination; multiple HarvestItems or media references never duplicate hits
Search loads no images or external resources and query counts stay bounded independently of result count
Exact Media navigation validates UUIDs and handles missing assets safely across refresh and browser history
Existing SEARCH-001 kinds remain covered; saved views, bulk operations and generic history remain deferred

features.description: Persist owner-private Saved operator views for existing search and directory controls
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated owner-private PostgreSQL SavedViews use UUIDv7, bounded normalized Unicode names, case-insensitive owner/surface uniqueness, UTC timestamps and an explicit state version

Finite surface contracts validate and canonicalize existing Global Search and directory state, reject unknown/transient keys and empty defaults, and retain exact stale UUID filters without new matching semantics
Owner-scoped list/create/rename/replace-state/delete APIs use normal Origin/CSRF/session protections and preserve safe management of unknown stored versions
Compact supported-surface controls and Dashboard access open ordinary canonical filter URLs with live results, offset zero, refresh/history safety and no implicit persistence after manual edits
Focused backend, real PostgreSQL/migration, frontend adapter/product/regression, generated API/static/build checks support operator UAT and independent final verification
No materialized results, arbitrary route or executable state, browser-local persistence, default views, sharing, bulk operations or unified history are introduced

features.description: Add explicit multi-selection and safe bulk Location moves for supported current collection records
acceptance_criteria: Active SeedLots, Sowings, Plants, PlantGroups and managed Stored material expose bounded transient explicit typed-ID selection with no query expansion or Saved View persistence

Authenticated Origin and CSRF protected preview validates every reference and existing scope-compatible Location, reports human labels, current and target Locations, no-ops and conflicts, and requires explicit confirmation
Apply locks and refreshes all selected records and target, revalidates UTC updated-at preconditions and domain eligibility, and commits all changes atomically or changes none

Domain-owned location assignment primitives preserve SeedLot and Sowing lineage and quantity and Stored material state, balance, correction version and dispositions; Plant and PlantGroup moves retain individual authoritative Movement Events

Responsive keyboard-accessible selection, toolbar and preview/apply dialog clear on navigation, filter or Saved View changes, refresh directory and Quick Preview state after success, and truthfully handle no-op and stale failures
Approved Overview, Collection, Activity, Places, Reference and Tools navigation groups and matching page eyebrows preserve all routes, page titles, descriptions and historical Event semantics

Focused backend, PostgreSQL atomicity and domain regressions, frontend selection and shell tests, generated API, static and production build checks prepare UAT; no migration, generic bulk framework, jobs, unified history or other bulk mutation is introduced

features.description: Add a read-only unified operational history over existing authoritative collection activity records
acceptance_criteria: Activity exposes distinct Journal and History destinations with permanent purpose copy, preserving the existing Event domain, events route and Saved View surface
Authenticated read-only History projects Events, propagation receipts, germination observations, structured Harvests, dispositions and seed conversions without a History or audit persistence table
Harvest-owned Events, Event-backed receipts and conversion-owned dispositions collapse to one user-visible operation
PartialDate precision is preserved, Recorded fallback is explicit, and deterministic ordering and timeline-year filtering use the date shown
Current state, updated_at, Supplier and provenance never fabricate history; Event and Harvest corrections update stable identities and ordinary Event deletion removes its projection
Retained reversals show supported status, with distinct reversal rows only for persisted reversal instants
Global SQL pagination, filtered totals, bounded limits and query counts remain correct across mixed-source pages without full-history hydration or N+1 queries
Typed primary and bounded related references derive exact existing authoritative deep links without stored arbitrary URLs
History Saved Views persist only validated stable filters, reopen on page one, and use a data-safe surface-constraint migration

Accessible desktop sidebar disclosures persist browser presentation preferences and reveal the active route; Journal hierarchy and History category chips, year controls, compact semantic timeline, loading/retry/empty states and counts fit desktop, tablet and mobile without changing filters, dates or mutation boundaries
